source.provenance: Bertrand-Mullainathan randomized resume correspondence experiment, AER ResumeNames snapshot

cases.question: What is the intention-to-treat effect of randomized Black-sounding rather than White-sounding names on employer callbacks?
cases.context: Names were randomly assigned to otherwise fictional resumes. treatment equals 1 for a Black-sounding name and 0 for a White-sounding name. callback is a post-assignment binary outcome, resume_id identifies a submitted resume, and baseline_experience is a pre-assignment resume attribute. Estimate ITT for treatment=1 versus treatment=0 at one row per submitted resume.

source.provenance: NHEFS complete-case observational smoking-cessation cohort from causaldata

cases.question: What is the ATE of quitting smoking by 1982 on weight change from 1971 to 1982?
cases.context: This is an observational cohort, not randomized. treatment is qsmk recoded as 1 for quitting and 0 for not quitting; weight_change is wt82_71 in kilograms; participant_id identifies a person. The approved pre-exposure adjustment set is age, sex, race, education, smokeintensity, smokeyrs, exercise, active, and wt71. Estimate ATE for treatment=1 versus treatment=0 in the frozen complete-case cohort. Positivity, consistency, and no unmeasured confounding remain assumptions.

source.provenance: Card-Krueger 1994 New Jersey/Pennsylvania fast-food restaurant survey archive

cases.question: What is the simultaneous-adoption DiD ATT of New Jersey's 1992 minimum-wage increase on restaurant full-time-equivalent employment?
cases.context: The source has one restaurant per record and two survey waves; the pinned transform makes a long panel. restaurant_id identifies a restaurant and is also the clustering unit, period is 0 before and 1 after, state is 1 for New Jersey and 0 for Pennsylvania, treatment is active exposure equal to 1 only for New Jersey after the increase, and fte_employment is the outcome. Adoption is period 1 for New Jersey; Pennsylvania is the comparison group. Use restaurant_id plus period grain. Parallel trends is required and is not proven by these two periods.

source.provenance: Ludwig-Miller Head Start county RDD data in the Calonico-Cattaneo-Farrell replication

cases.question: What is the local reduced-form effect at the Head Start poverty cutoff of grant-writing assistance eligibility on child mortality related to Head Start services?
cases.context: poverty_rate_1960 is the running variable, the fixed cutoff is exactly 59.1984, eligibility is assigned sharply at poverty_rate_1960 greater than or equal to 59.1984, treatment is that binary eligibility indicator, and child_mortality is the post-program outcome. county_id identifies a county and each row is one county. Estimate only the local sharp-RDD reduced-form effect of grant-writing assistance eligibility above versus below the cutoff, not the effect of funding, participation, or service receipt.
